name: Example Owner
team_size: 3 techs plus the owner and a part-time office helper
intro: This is an EXAMPLE of the page a real interview produces. Five things fit this made-up shop. Together they hand back about 9 to 16 hours a week. One the owner can set up tonight; the biggest ones need the phone and calendar hooked up.

facts.leads: Mostly phone calls from Google and repeat customers. Some web forms.
facts.missed_calls: About 6 to 10 calls a week go to voicemail while the owner is under a house. Callbacks happen at night.
facts.scheduling: Paper calendar in the truck and texts with the techs.
facts.quoting: Writes quotes at night from notes on his phone. About 5 a week.
facts.follow_up: Rarely follows up on quotes. Says he forgets.
facts.reviews: Asks for reviews when he remembers. Maybe once a month.
facts.back_office: Invoices in QuickBooks on Sunday nights. A few customers pay late.
facts.hates: Sunday night invoices and calling people back at 9 pm.

opportunities.name: Missed-call text back
opportunities.description: Every call you can't pick up gets a text back within a minute, asks what they need, and offers a time.
opportunities.why: EXAMPLE: The owner said 6 to 10 calls a week go to voicemail while he's on a job, and he calls back at night. Some of those people have already booked someone else.
opportunities.looks_like: A homeowner calls about a dead water heater at 10 am. Before they can dial the next company, they get a text from the shop, answer two questions, and pick a slot.
what_it_takes: A short list of services and service area
About an afternoon of setup with help, then it runs on its own
opportunities.top_reason: The calls you miss are the jobs you lose. This catches them.

opportunities.name: Quote follow-up
opportunities.description: Two days after a quote goes out, a friendly check-in goes to the customer in your words.
opportunities.why: EXAMPLE: About 5 quotes a week, and the owner said he rarely follows up because he forgets.
opportunities.looks_like: Thursday's quote gets a short text Saturday morning. The customer replies with a question instead of going quiet.
what_it_takes: Hooked to your texts or email
opportunities.top_reason: Quotes nobody follows up on are money left on the table.

opportunities.name: Invoice chaser
opportunities.description: Invoices go out when the job closes, and late ones get polite reminders on a schedule.
opportunities.why: EXAMPLE: Sunday nights go to QuickBooks invoices, and a few customers pay late every month.
opportunities.looks_like: Job closes Friday, invoice goes out Friday. Day 7, a friendly nudge. Day 14, a firmer one. Sunday night is free.

opportunities.name: Review request after every job
opportunities.description: The morning after a job, the customer gets a thank-you text with your Google review link.
opportunities.why: EXAMPLE: The owner asks for reviews about once a month, when he remembers.
opportunities.looks_like: Every finished job gets the same short thank-you the next morning. Reviews come in every week instead of now and then.
what_it_takes: A short thank-you in your words
An afternoon with a little help
opportunities.top_reason: More reviews means more calls from Google.

opportunities.name: Your business saved in ChatGPT
opportunities.description: Put your services, prices, area, and how you talk into ChatGPT's custom instructions once, so quotes come out right the first time.
opportunities.why: EXAMPLE: The audit found the owner re-explaining his business at the start of most quote chats.
opportunities.looks_like: He opens a new chat, types 'quote for a 50 gallon water heater swap, the Smith job,' and gets a draft in his own words.
what_it_takes: About ten minutes in ChatGPT settings, tonight, on your own
opportunities.top_reason: Ten minutes tonight, and every quote chat starts already knowing you.

closer: EXAMPLE: The top three need the phone, texts, and QuickBooks working together. That's a setup job, not something to paste in. On a twenty-minute call, Joey goes over these and what it takes to get them running.
